Approach and rationale The previous parent situation is highly local-optimum sensitive: the objective is the exact maximum over all discrete lags, and a good point usually has several lag constraints simultaneously active. A pure summed-gradient or single-stage SLSQP descent can either move mass against the wrong balance of active offsets or fail to make coordinated, box-feasible moves when several constraints participate. The plan below therefore changes the local search method and adds two complementary generator families: A. An exact linearized minimax local descent via a small LP per iteration. At each local step, the nonconvex minimax problem is replaced only for search-direction selection by the convex linear programming subproblem obtained by freezing current correlation values and using exact analytic Jacobians. The LP chooses a feasible tangent direction that is predicted to reduce the largest current correlations while not allowing nonactive correlations to gain too much. Every resulting point is repaired to the exact target sum and accepted only if the authoritative evaluator improves. B. A discrete balanced-sequence optimizer over 0/1 patterns (and explicit half-mass if the target sum is half-integral). In the original evaluator, a discrete improvement that is also nearly 0/1 can expose structure that continuous gradient methods miss, and it serves as an additional basin of attraction. Successful discrete states can be converted into feasible continuous states for further LP polishing. C. The parent, if supplied, is never copied numerically into the code and is not thrown away. It is used as the initial feasible archive, canonicalized, projected, interpolated to neighboring resolutions, read by the discrete pipeline, and used as the guaranteed fallback. Small-scale continuous interpolation and population averaging transfer parent structure without importing long numeric tables. This is not a global optimization proof. The exact objective is bilinear and nonconvex; LP substeps are only descent-direction surrogates and SLSQP local NLP polish is only a final refinement. The only accepted improvements are those of the original evaluator with the exact box and mass constraints. The method is materially different from the previous program: it does not rely on random multi-coordinate gradient plus random pair jumps as the main engine; it instead uses LP-generated tangent directions subject to the active offsets, adds exact discrete annealing, and applies stricter feasibility projection and cross-resolution ancestry. 2.
